research.title: Hybrid-CNN-ViT Architecture for Early Brain Tumor Detection
research.subtitle: Synergizing Deep Convolutional Feature Extraction with Vision Transformer Self-Attention for Multi-Sequence MRI Diagnosis
research.institution: Sonargaon University — Department of Computer Science & Engineering
research.abstract: Brain tumors present severe diagnostic challenges due to morphological heterogeneity and ambiguous tissue boundaries in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This research develops a novel Hybrid-CNN-ViT deep learning architecture that combines deep convolutional stems for granular edge/texture extraction with Vision Transformer multi-head self-attention mechanisms for global contextual dependency mapping across axial, coronal, and sagittal MRI brain slices.
research.dataset: Figshare & BraTS Multi-sequence MRI Benchmark (3,064+ T1-weighted, T2, FLAIR Scans)
research.targetTumors: Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary Tumors & Healthy Control Tissue

architectureSteps.description: Automated skull-stripping, intensity normalization (Z-score), contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE), and spatial augmentations to mitigate scanner variability.

architectureSteps.step: Phase 2: Deep CNN Spatial Feature Extractor
architectureSteps.description: High-resolution convolutional stem extracting granular low-level visual representations: subtle hyper-intensities, edema margins, and microscopic tumor boundaries.
Linear projection into patch embeddings with 12-layer multi-head self-attention blocks, capturing global structural relationships across disparate brain regions.
Dual-path cross-attention fusion layer synthesizing local and global embeddings, passing through MLP head for 4-class multi-label diagnosis with Grad-CAM explainability.
